quote.translation: In the third system, contingency was grasped in the dimension of nihility, as standing with impossibility in the relation of proximity that belongs to subalternation, and yet, for all that, it was understood as proclaiming its own actuality as the birth of the actual (see p. 237).

regions.text: 必然性との開係において、偶然性が單に必然性の否定ではなくして「必然性の餃如にも拘らずなほ事實性が現存してるる』ことが偶然性の不可鉄條件であることはマイノングも指摘してるる（Meinong,UiberMoglichkeitundWahrschcinlichkeit,1915，S.250）。

quote.translation: Meinong too points out that, in relation to necessity, it is an indispensable condition of contingency that it should be more than the negation of necessity, in that "despite the lack of necessity, factuality is nonetheless extant" (Meinong, Über Möglichkeit und Wahrscheinlichkeit, 1915, S. 240).

quote.translation: In relation to possibility, as Hegel says, contingency is nothing other than "immediate actuality" (unmittelbare Wirklichkeit).

quote.translation: The contingent is precisely "a determinate being" (ein Dasein), "an existence" (eine Existenz), "an immediate" (ein Unmittelbares) (Hegel, Encyklopädie, hrsg. v. Bolland, 1906, § 146 u. Zusatz).

quote.translation: Contingency, in short, is the actuality of the actual as the merely actual.

regions.text: シェリングの云ふが如く偶然とは「在るとだけ云へる』（nursagen,dassesIst）ものである。「豚義の事象』（dasGeschchenexar®Goyt）である（Scheling,SammticheWerke,1856-1857,I,1,S.464,E,2,S.153）。

quote.translation: As Schelling says, the contingent is that of which "one can only say that it Is" (nur sagen, dass es Ist), "what happens in the eminent sense" (das Geschehene κατ' ἐξοχήν) (Schelling, Sämmtliche Werke, 1856-1857, II, 1, S. 464, II, 2, S. 153).

regions.text: さうして、偶然性の時間性格たる現在性もまた實に單なる現實としての偶然の現實性に基いたるのである。

quote.translation: And presentness, as the temporal character of contingency, is also in truth based on the actuality of the contingent as the merely actual.
